Trust and limits

Five properties every change is judged against, what each one promises, what Sigma refuses to do when it cannot be sure.

On this page
  • The five properties
  • What it refuses when unsure
  • What fails open, said plainly
  • What is advice, not enforcement
  • Known threats, from the threat model
  • What leaves your machine

Most people only need

  • When Sigma cannot be sure, it stops and says so instead of carrying on weaker.
  • It merges and spends only where you opted in.
  • Its limits are derived from your machine, not copied constants.
  • Read What fails open before you trust an unattended run.
  • What leaves your machine is a short section.

Sigma runs on developer machines and can change code and GitHub. So the rule is: when it cannot be sure, it stops and says so, instead of carrying on with a weaker guarantee. It spends and merges only where you opted in, and it limits itself by what your machine can bear.

The five properties

PropertyThe promiseWhat it looks like
ReliabilityIt does what it claims.No capability is described as working until it has run end to end in the real target environment. A performance or resource claim carries the measurement behind it.
ScalabilityIt holds as machines, repositories and data grow.Per-item costs are stated at 10x and 100x; single chokepoints are named as ceilings with a number; unbounded growth is a defect at design time. GitHub quota is watched, and a rate-limited read stops the run rather than guessing.
ResiliencyIt recovers without a human.Every failure mode has a stated recovery: a stopped run resumes where it left off, a dead session's unstarted claims are released, a lease expires, a stale ledger re-roots with one command. Retries are idempotent or bounded, and a recovery lever must not itself cause an outage.
SafetyIt cannot harm the host, the data or your trust.Resource limits are derived from the machine, not copied constants. Nothing spawns a background process, sends data or uses quota without you opting in. Secrets stay out of config files, logs and shell history. Where a guarantee cannot be made on a platform, it refuses loudly.
LivenessIt is running when it should be, and you can tell.A long-running piece reports its own health where you will see it, and a dead one reads differently from one with nothing to do: age is the tell, not an error count. Revival is layered, so a missed trigger costs latency, never data.A heartbeat shows the process is alive, not that it is healthy. Nothing restarts the Slack listener for you.

What it refuses when unsure

SituationWhat Sigma does
Branch protection cannot be readUnder work.auto_merge: always the merge stops and names the lever; retrying merges nothing until protection can be read. "Nothing is enforced" is claimed only when both the classic API and the rulesets answered nothing.
GitHub reports an unknown merge stateAn unknown state never reads as clean. The goal parks.
Merge rights cannot be determined, or the pull request is a fork'sIt never attempts the merge. The pull request stays open and the goal is recorded review, not done.
The comment list or the review list is unreadableThe merge parks.
A goal is claimed finished before its pull request mergedrecord done is refused unless one read confirms the merge. An open or unreadable pull request is recorded review.
No passing verify evidence from this run, when verify is requiredrecord done and the merge are refused.
A staged path or added line looks like a credentialThe commit verb refuses and names it.
A plan has no approved plan-review for its exact bytesrecord done and the merge are refused; with the opt-in gate, so is the pull-request push.
The machine has no roomA hold with a reason and a retry time; the goal is not failed. On Windows the guard refuses rather than guess.
The ledger's publish lock cannot be madeThe publish verbs refuse and defer, naming the override variable.
Slack listener is off or has no channel idIt refuses to start.
A repository supplies a command, git option or symlinked stateRefused unless you opt in. Verify trust is granted per checkout and not committed.

What fails open, said plainly

  • Under work.require_review: changes, an unreadable review decision and the unresolved-thread count fail open; the comment and review lists fail closed.
  • Every ledger call fails open: a ledger problem never stops a run, by design.
  • The edit-time plan gate, the decision-registry hook and the issue-priority hook fail open on their own errors, and exist on Claude Code only.
  • The merge-bypass setting work.merge_bypass is off unless set to the exact string ruleset. It is the one place Sigma merges past a rule GitHub reports, and it trusts that the person who set it meant it; nothing in code can tell an operator's edit of the config from an agent's.

What is advice, not enforcement

Some controls are instructions to the agent that no code checks:

  • Independent review. The skills ask for an author-blind reviewer. The core cannot prove the maker did not influence it, and a maker can record its own approving verdict.
  • Irreversible actions park. The agent is asked to park a deploy, delete, overwrite, spend or migrate. Code checks it only when the hard-stop rulebook is switched on (off by default).

Rules enforced by plain Python behave the same on every host. Rules enforced by a hook exist on Claude Code only; Sigma uses no Cursor hooks. A hook is an accelerator, never load-bearing.

Known threats, from the threat model

ThreatResidual riskState
Prompt injection: an issue or comment asks a phase agent to run a command or edit labelshighno technical mitigation at that crossing; an open issue tracks it
A notification webhook pointed at an Internet host instead of a local adapterhighno technical mitigation; the webhook is opt-in
A Slack --unsafe-merge from the authorised channelmediumchannel membership is the only authority
A token-shaped value reaching a log or commentmediumknown patterns are scrubbed
A dead watcher mistaken for an idle onemediuma session-start staleness check and the doctor warn; they do not make a stopped process healthy

Do not run an unattended loop on a repository you do not trust: it can carry its own .sdlc/config.json.

What leaves your machine

Sigma reports no usage data. Opt-in destinations only: Slack (SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN), a configured webhook, a configured SMTP server, and model calls through your agent host. GitHub traffic goes through gh. The action log, timing store and phase transcripts stay on your machine. Your agent host talks to its own model provider, which is outside Sigma's control.
